answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by making voting and payout rights depend on a slowly earned work record, not on cheap new keys. Each identity has to keep a public lantern of recent tasks that independent peers have scored, and those records sit on a shared mesa that anyone can audit. A farm that tries to flood the market at the nadir of a quiet epoch still has to fill a lantern for every alias, so spinning up empty names stops being cheaper than doing the work once under one identity.
